title: How do the counts change when the game goes to nine hundred?
description: The game is played till nine hundred instead of ninety. Sharing nine hundred into groups of three, five and fifteen shows that every count becomes ten times as large.
teaching_notes: One idea: nine hundred is ten times ninety, so each count of multiples is ten times as large. Watch for students who add instead of multiplying by ten.

source: Figure it Out box 1, Q3, p.108
video_script.why: The child counts the multiples of three, five and fifteen up to nine hundred and sees that each count is ten times as large as before.
video_script.substitution: Count the multiples up to nine hundred by sharing nine hundred into groups, and compare with ninety.
video_script.anchor: children playing the idli-vada game, now till nine hundred
video_script.payoff_line: Idli is said three hundred times, vada one hundred and eighty times, and idli-vada sixty times

final_answer.value: idli-vada 60 times, vada 180 times, idli 300 times; each answer is 10 times as large
final_answer.spoken: idli is said three hundred times, vada one hundred and eighty times, and idli-vada sixty times

never_show: idli 30 times as the new answer
video_script.design: One idea: when the limit is ten times as big, each count of multiples is ten times as big. Same method as the earlier example: share the limit into groups.
